rationale:
Evidence: all 480 development trials (iterations 0-8) ended off track after one line-loss event, with max_error about 0.061 m against the 0.06 m limit. That limit is the floor for any body_width up to 0.18 m, so widening the body cannot help. Progress stayed at 0.04 to 0.15 across gain, mass, line-loss and sensor-spacing changes. Only forward sensor placement (y 0.06 to 0.08) and the 7-sensor array moved s-bend and slalom progress. Iteration 9 (speed 0.8, kd 1.0, footprint 0.012) never raced, so its result is unknown.

My hypothesis is that the failure is a slip-out at the first bend. At base_speed 1.0 the robot carries too much speed into the curve for its turn authority, so it runs wide and loses the tape. Survival matters more than pace here: the score is dominated by 250*progress, and a robot that stays on track for the full 3.0 s at moderate speed scores far above the current 50. A robot that completes is worth more still, but it has to survive first.

Changes: (1) base_speed 1.0 to 0.7 to reduce slip-out at bends. (2) Keep the iteration 4 sensing that gave the best s-bend result: 7 sensors at y = 0.08 m, x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, footprint 0.016 m, linear antisymmetric weights. (3) kp 2.0 unchanged, to keep steering authority at the lower speed. (4) kd 0.6 to 0.8 for more damping of the swing after a line loss. (5) ki 0.05 kept, so the integral stays small. (6) Mass 0.6 kg, wheel_track 0.14 m and body unchanged, and line_loss search_right kept since it gave the best score so far.

Expected result: max_error below 0.06 m on at least the s-bend and oval, with the first line loss moving later or disappearing. Progress should rise toward 0.3 to 0.6. Completion within 3 s is unlikely at 0.7 base speed, so the score gain depends on survival rather than finishing. If the failure point stays fixed at about progress 0.115 on the oval, the cause is the start or the track geometry rather than speed.
